## Research question

How do target-site indel-bearing read fractions compare between a Cas9 example
and a control? This notebook uses **synthetic data** for learning Quarto.

Cas9 uses guide RNA to direct DNA cleavage [@jinek2012]. RNA-directed Cas9
cleavage at genomic loci in mammalian cells was demonstrated by @cong2013.
These studies provide biological background. Our invented counts illustrate
how to combine code, research notes, and references in one document.

## Code and descriptive results

One row in `counts.csv` represents one synthetic sample. The denominator is
all target-site reads in that sample. Report the indel-bearing read fraction
as a percentage, then calculate a descriptive mean across samples per condition.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

counts = pd.read_csv("counts.csv")
assert counts["sample"].is_unique
assert (counts["total_reads"] > 0).all()
assert counts["indel_reads"].between(0, counts["total_reads"]).all()
counts["indel_percent"] = 100 * counts.indel_reads / counts.total_reads
print(counts.to_string(index=False))
means = counts.groupby("condition")["indel_percent"].mean()
for condition, mean in means.items():
    print(f"{condition}: mean indel-bearing reads = {mean:.1f}%")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-indels
#| fig-cap: "Synthetic target-site indel fractions, three samples per condition."
#| fig-alt: "Control samples have 2, 3, and 1 percent indel-bearing reads. Cas9 samples have 40, 45, and 50 percent. All six samples have 100 target-site reads."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
colors = counts["condition"].map({"Control": "#666666", "Cas9": "#287a9b"})
ax.bar(counts["sample"], counts["indel_percent"], color=colors)
ax.set_xlabel("Synthetic sample (C: control; T: Cas9)")
ax.set_ylabel("Indel-bearing reads (%)")
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Research notes

The group means describe these invented inputs. They provide no evidence about
biological efficacy. Reads within a sample are not independent biological
replicates. Equal weighting of samples defines the descriptive group mean here.

An indel-bearing read fraction does not establish an edited-cell percentage,
a precise intended edit, functional knockout, or off-target specificity.
A real study would need assay definitions, controls, and independent biological
replicates. This example supplies no organism, target gene, or guide sequence.
